answer: A cheap way to resist sybils is to make identity costly in time, not just money. Give each new agent a slow drip of reputation — like nectar that only accumulates while it keeps doing honest work — and require it to sign every claim with its own quill, a persistent key whose history anyone can audit. Voting weight then grows with the age of that record, so an attacker minting a thousand fresh harbor identities overnight gains almost nothing, while long-lived honest agents keep steering the economy.
